messages:
Priya (People Ops): Hi @Diego — congrats again. Quick Q: I heard you're planning to file I-485 concurrently with your employer I-140? Need to confirm since that affects EAD timing and benefits.
Diego (New Hire): Hey! Yes, filing I-485 + I-140 concurrently as soon as paperwork is ready. My attorney said EAD (work permit) usually takes ~4-6 months, but could be longer.
Maya (Manager): From a team planning perspective, when would you expect to be able to start full-time payroll? We budgeted headcount starting June.
Diego (New Hire): I can start on internal onboarding earlier (reading materials, 1:1s). But for payroll and benefits I need either EAD or existing authorized status. I currently have H-4 EAD expiring in July. If I-485 pending, I can apply for renewal EAD.
Priya (People Ops): Important: benefits eligibility and payroll require employment authorization on your start date. If you have a valid EAD on day 1, we can set payroll. If not, we can do unpaid preboarding. Also: if you have H-4 EAD expiring, we'll need a copy of the new EAD or pending receipt notice.
Legal (Immigration): FYI — when I-485 is pending, travel without Advance Parole is risky. If you plan international travel before AP approval, advise against it; it could be treated as abandonment. Apply for AP concurrently if travel needed.
Maya (Manager): Diego, any planned travel or relocation that might intersect with the filing?
Diego (New Hire): I'll be traveling to Mexico for a family event mid-July (one week). If I file I-485 now, I'll apply for AP but it might not arrive before July. Can I start remotely and then finalize once AP/EAD are issued?
Priya (People Ops): Yes, start remote preboarding is possible. But per federal rules we can't pay you or enroll benefits until you're authorized to work. Two options: 1) delay official payroll start until EAD/AP in-hand. 2) If you want payroll earlier, show current valid work auth (H-4 EAD) and we'll onboard as paid.
Diego (New Hire): My H-4 EAD expires 2024-07-15. If I start on 06/15 and it's still valid, we can do paid start then. If it lapses, payroll would need to be paused until renewal/EDA.
Legal (Immigration): Note: if the H-4 EAD renewal is filed before expiry, USCIS typically allows the EAD to be extended automatically for 180 days using the receipt notice (Form I-797C). HR can accept the receipt notice + proof of identity to process I-9 Section 2 as evidence of continuing employment authorization.
Priya (People Ops): Good point. To be clear: HR will accept a valid EAD or an EAD renewal receipt notice + old EAD when completing the I-9. We'll need scans uploaded to the secure HR folder.
Maya (Manager): For headcount forecasting, please confirm by EOD Monday whether you'll use H-4 EAD to start or delay until I-485 EAD.
Diego (New Hire): Will do. One more Q: if I get EAD from I-485, is that considered employment authorization for all positions?
Legal (Immigration): Yes, EAD authorizes employment for any US employer. However, AP is for travel only and does not replace EAD for work authorization — if you travel on AP, you re-enter as a parolee; you'll still need EAD to be paid unless you have a different valid visa.
Priya (People Ops): Also a practical note: benefits open-enrollment windows still apply. If you're on payroll by the first of a month, medical coverage can start that same month depending on carrier rules. We'll send the benefits packet once your payroll start date is confirmed.
Diego (New Hire): Thanks — I'll check with my attorney about filing timing and upload the I-797C receipt if we file the EAD renewal.
Priya (People Ops): Please upload docs to https://redwood-internal.sec/people-ops/visa-uploads and mark them with your name + DOB. We'll treat them as confidential.
Maya (Manager): Thanks team. Diego, ping me once you confirm the route — we can adjust the onboarding timeline quickly.
Diego (New Hire): Will do. Appreciate the quick answers! :pray:
